Condo Buying Checklist for Phuket

Print it, take it to the viewing
HomeGuidesCondo Buying Checklist for Phuket

Buying property · Last reviewed: 2026-11-23

Use this checklist before you reserve or sign. Not every point applies to every project. Items marked with a legal topic are best checked with an independent lawyer.

The project and developer

  • Developer name, registered company and previous completed projects.
  • Advertised completion date and the history of that developer meeting dates.
  • Is the building completed, under construction or pre-sale?
  • Who runs building management after handover?

Title, quota and legal

  • Land title of the project and the building permit, verified by your lawyer.
  • Foreign quota remaining in the building if you are a foreign buyer.
  • Freehold or leasehold: for leasehold, term, renewal wording and registration.
  • Reservation agreement and sale and purchase agreement read by your lawyer before signing.
  • What the booking fee and deposits are, and when they are refundable.

The unit

  • Exact unit number, floor, size and whether the size is internal or includes balcony and common share.
  • Orientation and view; check on site, not only in the render.
  • Furniture and fittings included, listed in writing.
  • Parking: included or extra.
  • Noise sources: road, nightlife, construction next door, air-conditioning plant.

Costs

  • Total price, what the price includes and the currency.
  • Transfer fee and taxes: amount and who pays.
  • Common area fee and sinking fund: amount, billing basis and what it covers.
  • Utilities set-up and deposits.
  • Legal fees and bank charges.

On the viewing

  • Water pressure, air conditioning, damp or leaks, window and door fit.
  • Lifts, corridors and pool maintenance in completed buildings.
  • Walk to the nearest beach, shop and clinic to see the real distance. The Nearby section on each project page lists distances, many of them straight-line.
  • Ask about rental rules and whether short stays are allowed in the building.

Before you pay

  • Money moves through the route your lawyer and bank confirm, with the foreign exchange documents kept.
  • Every promise from the sales team is in the contract.
  • You have had at least one night to think and to read the contract.

Frequently asked questions

Do I need a lawyer?

We recommend an independent Thai lawyer for title checks and for reading the contract, especially for off-plan purchases.

Are short-term rentals always allowed in a condo?

No. Building rules and local regulations can restrict short-term rental. Ask the juristic person and your lawyer before you count on rental income.
